items.title: Eight Bits of Trust: eMudhra's CA keys cracked in milliseconds
items.content: Eight Bits of Trust; eMudhra's CA keys cracked in milliseconds Home Speaking Training Media Contact Sponsor 🌙 Subscribe Sponsored by: Report URI - XSS can ride a passkey-authenticated session. See it in the browser. Certificate Authorities Eight Bits of Trust; eMudhra's CA keys cracked in milliseconds Scott Helme Security researcher, entrepreneur and international speaker who specialises in web technologies. More posts by Scott Helme. Scott Helme 20 Oct 2026 • 7 min read One of eMudhra's certificate authority private keys is the number 4. Not a number that starts with 4, or the number 4 followed by a few hundred random digits, just, 4... Another one is 56, and another is 115. I know, because I recovered all of them from their public certificates on my laptop just now, and it took less than a second. What happened On Saturday 17th October a security researcher reported to Apple, Google, Microsoft, Mozilla and eMudhra that the private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were compromised. Chrome pushed a CRLSet update blocking them that evening and Mozilla blocked them in Firefox via OneCRL a few hours later. On Tuesday 20th, Mozilla announced it publicly and shipped an NSS update removing the eMudhra root, and Chrome confirmed the root is going in Chrome Root Store v43. The eight intermediates are six TLS issuing CAs (DV, OV and EV, two generations each) and two code-signing CAs, all created in April 2025. Every one of them was also cross-signed by Sectigo's AAA Certificate Services root in May 2025. That's the "what", but it's the "how" that's the interesting part, and it was summed up in one line on the thread by Ian Carroll: They are inherently weak single-byte keys that anyone can factor, and the issue cannot be contained. What a private key actually is These are elliptic-curve keys on the P-384 curve. The private key is just a number, d . The public key, the thing that goes in the certificate for the world to see, is d × G , where G is a fixed point
items.author: hkc
items.summary_zh: 安全研究者 Scott Helme 发现，eMudhra 一张中间 CA 证书的私钥就是数字 4，另外几张分别是 56 和 115；他在自己的笔记本上从公开证书里取回全部私钥，用时不到一秒。10 月 17 日有研究者向 Apple、Google、Microsoft、Mozilla 和 eMudhra 报告八张中间证书私钥泄露，Chrome 当晚推送 CRLSet 拦截，Firefox 数小时后经 OneCRL 屏蔽。
items.summary_en: Scott Helme recovered the private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate certificates straight from their public certificates in under a second, because the keys were tiny integers such as 4, 56 and 115. The compromise was reported to Apple, Google, Microsoft, Mozilla and eMudhra on 17 October; Chrome shipped a CRLSet block that evening and Firefox followed hours later through OneCRL.

items.title: Docker is weird
items.content: Code and Cake - Docker is weird Code and Cake Follow About me Docker is weird Oct 22, 2026 I decided to make my own container runtime for fun, and even though I’m still early on, I’ve learned that Docker is weird . Here’s some weird things I learned about Docker. Containers aren’t real Unlike VMs, containers are just processes with special restrictions on them. Your kernel is still running that process! And if you know where to look, you can even find that process in /proc. Containers really aren’t real There’s not really a linux feature that’s just “containers” either. Instead, containers are really 5 different linux kernel features in trenchcoat. Namespaces hide what the host and container can see, cgroups limit container resource usage, and there’s a whole bunch of networking magic I don’t understand that lets you isolate a container’s network. Images are just folders Images are just folders that Docker puts somewhere and then calls chroot (or pivot_root ) to make that folder your container process’s new root directory. So if you run docker run -it --rm ubuntu /bin/bash , Docker is going to: Download the ubuntu image from Dockerhub. Put that image somewhere. Run /some/weird/docker/path/bin/bash Go is kind of a terrible language for a container runtime Docker’s container runtime, runc , is written in Go, and Go has some design choices that make it less suited for a container runtime. Go’s runtime is natively multi-threaded. That’s a really cool feature, but it leads to some challenges in runc . Many of the Linux syscalls a container runtime needs to make have to be done in a single-threaded environment, so runc has a crazy C module that runs before Go’s runtime initializes so it can run those syscalls. Go also doesn’t have fork! Fork only forks the main thread, so it’s kind of a footgun in a runtime like Go’s. But a container runtime really wants to fork, set up a bunch of restrictions, and then exec the process you actually put in docker run . To get around this,

items.title: Jailbreaking the Switch 2
items.content: Sammy Hajhamid — Blog ??? blog jailbreaking the switch 2 ns2jb is a software-only jailbreak of the switch 2 for the current latest firmware 23.0.1 October 18, 2026 cs Introduction You can get a copy of the exploit from the ns2jb repository. ns2jb is a software-only, tethered jailbreak for the Switch 2. It allows running arbitrary native code as any ordinary sysmodule, and as the built-in fs sysmodule. This lets us run homebrew, reverse engineer and mod Switch 2 games, back up save files off the Switch, and access most of the Switch 2’s peripherals through MMIO. To my knowledge, it’s the first such exploit for the Switch 2. To demonstrate the capabilities of this jailbreak, Codex modded a Switch 2 exclusive, Mario Kart World. Thanks to my friends in Dabney House who helped me choose characters to add and playtest the game. No, it’s just a silly caption. I set a /goal for userland code execution, but that didn’t succeed. The jailbreak itself took substantial effort for ~2 weeks. The Mario Kart World, however, was entirely vibecoded in a day, and was just for fun. The JetKVMs allow Codex to send controller inputs to the Switches over USB and receive video output over HDMI. We also need a way to press the power button—when the Switch 2 crashes, it needs a button press to restart. That’s what the Bluetooth light switch flicker from Amazon is for. items.content: I posted here about the then-upcoming PHP RCEs related to CVE-2026-109618 & CVE-2026-109619. I appreciate this has had considerable knock-on effects with the schedule for co-ordinated disclosure, and created additional workload. I am truly sorry. I take full responsibility for my actions. It was not remotely my intention to cause any of the subsequent side effects. At the time of posting, I didn't know about any embargo. My contact had told me there was no embargo, and her contact had told her the same thing. As someone who follows the 4-weekly PHP release cycle and compiles it from source, my intention was to alert others in a similar position to be aware of the importance/urgency of the updates. items.title: Show HN: OnKey – I'm a bad singer, so I built an app to show where I'm off-key
items.content: Hi all I was pretty terrible at singing, now I’d say I’m bad but not terrible. This is because I’ve been using a singing app (won’t name it here) that scores me on my pitch and timing throughout the song so that I can improve. Lately however, the app I’ve been using has flooded their song list with songs that aren’t originals. I didn’t like this at all as for me, it’s easier to try to improve when you’re singing along to the original. So, I asked an agent (Claude Code) if it could write some code to listen to Spotify and also listen to me and see if it could detect both pitches and score me. It impressed me by writing some Python and showing me my pitch in the terminal! It couldn’t go all the way though and detect the singer’s pitch in real time. So I found the next best setup and built OnKey, a Mac app that needs to listen to the song once (it doesn’t save it) and then when it’s learnt the song (takes a couple of minutes), you can sing along to the pitch track that it’s learnt. OnKey is free to use and open source under the MIT license. It can listen to Spotify, Apple Music, and YouTube playing in your browser with the right permissions. During the build I found that someone had done something similar in Nightingale, but this requires a library of songs exported to disk and who has this in 2026 (maybe some of you ;) - but we need to help the normies too). You can check out a demo video on the site of me singing (warning given) here: https://singonkey.app The app sends out to find the song info (short Shazam fingerprint, and looks up song details), lyrics (from LRCLIB), and checks for updates. The app never sends the music (it doesn’t save this to disk) and your voice. Everything you’d expect to stay private does. It’s still weak in a few places: - when the song’s backing is noisy it’s hard to pick the pitch track out - sometimes it gets a note an octave off - it’s limited to Apple Silicon Macs, M1 or later, and only macOS 14.2 up because extra drivers aren’t requir

items.title: Show HN: Corgi, a helpful {agent, terminal} multiplexer
items.content: Hey everyone, Inspired by Herdr, I've built an agent multiplexer that I've been using as my daily driver for a few weeks now. I think I improved on the concept in a few ways, focusing on the ergonomics I always wished I had: I show you what the agents are up to, along with a running feed of their activity. There's also a simple shortcut (F1) to go to the next unread agent. I use multiple accounts, so I've added unified launcher for Codex/Claude Code/Pi. Theres some careful ergonomics there: fast search and resume over sessions, inline usage tracking etc. Many small quality of life improvements to the terminal experience: - Links can be copied with a click, so no need to drag-select over many lines - cmd+v just pastes images (even on SSH) - images have a thumbnail preview. - Built-in CPU/Memory/GPU usage tracking, broken down by workspace I assume you have access to cheap inference (Luna/Haiku/etc). It just reuses the agents to organize things for you: what is this http link? what is this worktree about? what is each agent doing? It's small but it made my environment feel more cozy. On a personal note, I've been on a frustrating sick leave for a while now. I created Corgi to challenge myself, and see if I can go back. The answer is more mixed than I had hoped, but I am happy with the result and thankful for the experience. I hope you like it! a few friends & myself have been using it for a few weeks and it's been pretty nice. There's still a lot to improve and some rough edges, so feedback would be greatly appreciated. Thank you :)

items.title: Show HN: Uberblok – an interactive museum of ZFS internals
items.content: I've worked for a long time in the storage field during my career and ZFS is the piece of engineering I admire most in that space. I wanted a way to pay homage to it and to explore and better understand its internals. So I built Uberblok: a museum of ZFS. A deep dive into copy-on-write, txgs, vdevs, RAID-Z, snapshots, the ARC, metaslabs, the ZIL, send/receive with explanations and animated diagrams. I'm sure people here know these internals better than I do, so corrections are very welcome. I built it with my agent swarm organization, Algotitan. I hope you'll enjoy the deep dive into Uberblok as much as I do. Museum: https://uberblok.storagebits.workers.dev Repo: https://github.com/algotitanhq/uberblok

items.title: Show HN: Omnara – Open-source alternative to Claude Managed Agents
items.content: Hey all, Kartik from Omnara ( https://omnara.com ) here. We're building an open-source API for running durable agents. You create an agent with an API call, and Omnara runs the agent loop, gives the agent sandboxes to run commands in, and handles secrets, permissions, and RBAC. Each agent's state is stored in Postgres, so agents survive restarts and cost nothing while idle. You can message them and stream their events over the API. You may remember us from our early days, when we made a remote-control phone app for Claude Code and Codex. Since the harness ran on a laptop back then, we had to build a relay to reach it, it stopped when the laptop closed, and moving it to a cloud sandbox meant syncing code and agent state between machines. We didn't think remote-controlling a local agent was end-game for how people would run agents, so we built a new product where the agent runs in the cloud, any client can talk to it through an API, and it can still use your laptop as one of its machines. Anthropic and OpenAI are building hosted versions of this, like Claude Managed Agents and the OpenAI Agents API. Omnara is an open-source version you can run on your own servers and use your own models. It's basically a harness server like the opencode or codex servers, but durable, scalable, with the usual harness features like file and shell tools, subagents, compaction, permission prompts, MCP, skills, memory, yada yada yada. Here's some interesting architectural decisions we made while building this out: Most harnesses, like Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, Goose, etc, run the agent loop in one long-lived process that keeps its log in a JSONL or SQLite file. In Omnara, the log is an append-only event log in Postgres, with inputs, model outputs and tool calls stored as typed rows in their own tables. items.title: Show HN: Impossible Machines: declaratively program the physical world
items.content: Hey all — Sharing a thought experiment I put together. The premise: what might declarative programming feel like for the physical world? We’re already familiar with this paradigm in software land (eg SQL etc where we declare what we want and the execution engine figures out how). I didn’t have access to an actuator so I mocked up the concept in software. The way it works is you demonstrate the effect and the system figures out how to achieve it. So say you want to ring a bell and you have a crank. The system will find a way to connect the two. If you add obstacles it figures out how to work around them (runs a constraint solver runs behind the scenes). I think what’s interesting about this is being able to think about the problem at a higher level of abstraction, with the system figuring out a way to achieve the intended effect. Anyways, curious to read reactions, feedback, and interesting ideas on how to extend this!

items.title: Show HN: Swurf – Swipe through the real web
items.content: Hello HN, Swurf allows you to swipe through the real web one page after another. It learns what you like and doesn’t show you the same page twice. The idea came naturally: there’s a seemingly infinite amount of high quality blog posts, random topic rabbit holes, and trending or cool sites that exist which the average person simply will never load on their browser. Swurf solves that by allowing you to rapidly traverse a constantly growing and learning feed of sites that it thinks you’d want to view. Quickly sift through endless pages and find things you like - effortlessly. One of the core drivers for making this project was the desire for real content. The project started as a simple tool for myself to find new and interesting things to learn and read about. Hours spent scrolling on my phone - while it still has its place - is increasingly losing its sense of reward. It’s genuinely hard to put into words exactly how swurfin’ feels but it’s almost refreshing in a sense. I encourage you to try it out and provide feedback. At this time there are no accounts and you can jump in and start swurfin’ immediately. There is a three dot menu button on the bottom right which allows you to submit links, save links, control adult content, and search similar topics. One of the things that’s great about Swurf is that its almost like a group browsing session (though entirely private) where everyone else who is spending time hunting down great reads or solid sites is helping massage the feed for you and you for them - all within your own set of interests. Enjoy and please ask any questions you have as theres plenty of room to grow.

items.title: Launch HN: Alter (YC S25) – Access control for multi-user agents
items.content: Hi HN! We’re Srikar and Kevan, founders of Alter – https://alterauth.com/ . We’re building access control for agents that can take actions on behalf of multiple users. If you’ve built an internal agent people use through Slack, you may have experienced this scenario: everyone signs in with their own account, but the agent connects to the CRM or billing system with one shared API key, so the agent can do anything that the key can do. User-level authentication in Slack does nothing to control what the agent can do in an external system like the CRM or billing system. Here’s what Alter does: -It acts as a proxy and manages downstream credentials for every API request that an agent takes; -It takes identity into account for every action the agent does. Automatically take into account the end user identity of the person that the agent is taking actions on behalf of. -It enforces fine grained runtime policies and records compliance grade audit logs. Here’s a demo video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9ZqPU14ipGE We started this because we saw first hand how hard it is to build agents in regulated industries. To unlock the true benefits of agents we need to allow agents to take actions, sometimes actions on behalf of end users. I (Srikar) was working at Goldmans and I saw how prohibitively expensive it was for me as a developer to write my own custom auth to enable multi-tenancy in agents and to allow agents to have strict policy controls as they act on behalf of end users. items.title: cloudflare/security-audit-skill
items.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings
items.readme:
# security-audit

A coding-agent skill that turns your agent into a security auditor. It orchestrates isolated agents through reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting.

This is the skill that seeded Cloudflare's vulnerability discovery harness, described in [Build your own vulnerability harness](https://blog.cloudflare.com/build-your-own-vulnerability-harness). The harness grew into a multi-stage, fleet-wide system; this skill is the single-repo starting point it evolved from.

## What it does

The skill runs a structured audit in six phases:

1. **Reconnaissance** -- map architecture, trust boundaries, input surfaces, prior evidence, and deterministic coverage in `architecture.md` and `coverage-ledger.json`.
2. **Coverage-led hunting** -- assign isolated hunters from ledger units, record their checks, and use coverage critics to find gaps.
3. **Candidate validation** -- give every unique candidate to a fresh verifier that tries to disprove it.
4. **Structured output** -- write `confirmed`, `needs_validation`, and `rejected` records to `findings.json` and validate them against `report-schema.json`.
5. **Independent record verification** -- fresh agents verify final source claims. Material replacements receive another independent verifier.
6. **Target-neutral reporting** -- derive `REPORT.md`, `FINDINGS-DETAIL.md`, and `NEEDS-VALIDATION.md` from the verified records and coverage ledger.

The parent runs `validate-coverage-ledger.cjs` after creating the ledger and after each later ledger update. It runs `validate-findings.cjs` in Phase 4 and again after every Phase 5 replacement.

The verdicts are distinct: `confirmed` has a complete source trace and bounded observed result, `needs_validation` has an exact unresolved fact and no severity, and `rejected` records a disproved candidate.

# Agent Toolkit for AWS

[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Build](https://github.com/aws/agent-toolkit-for-aws/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/aws/agent-toolkit-for-aws/actions/workflows/build.yml)
[![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-GA-green.svg)](https://github.com/aws/agent-toolkit-for-aws)

Help AI coding agents build, deploy, and manage applications on AWS.

The Agent Toolkit for AWS gives AI coding agents the tools, knowledge, and guardrails they need to work with AWS services. It works with the coding agents developers already use — including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Devin, Kiro, and fx.

## Quick start

### AWS CLI

Use the Agent Toolkit directly from your terminal with the AWS CLI:

```
aws configure agent-toolkit
```

See the [AWS CLI integration guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/agent-toolkit/latest/userguide/aws-cli.html) for setup, configuration, and usage instructions.

### Claude Code

The plugins are available on the official Anthropic marketplace (`claude-plugins-official`) which is added to your Claude Code installation by default.
Use the following commands to install supported plugins from the toolkit:

For `aws-core` that covers service selection, CDK/CloudFormation, serverless, containers, storage, observability, billing, SDK usage, and deployment:

```
/plugin install aws-core@claude-plugins-official
```

> **Tip:** If you get `Plugin not found`, update your local marketplace index first:
>
> ```
> /plugin marketplace update claude-plugins-official
> ```

For `aws-agents` that covers building AI agents on AWS with Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore:

```
/plugin install aws-agents@claude-plugins-official
```

For `aws-data-analytics` that covers data lake, analytics, and ETL workflows with S3 Tables, AWS Glue, and Athena:

```
/plugin install aws-data-analytics@claude-plugins-official
```

items.readme:
# Impeccable

Design guidance for AI coding agents. 1 skill, 24 commands, live browser iteration, and 62 deterministic detector rules for AI-generated frontend design.

> **Quick start:** From your project root, run `npx impeccable install`, then run `/impeccable init` inside your AI coding tool. Full docs: [impeccable.style](https://impeccable.style).

## Why Impeccable?

Anthropic's [frontend-design](https://github.com/anthropics/skills/tree/main/skills/frontend-design) was the first widely-used design skill for Claude. Impeccable started from there.

Every model trained on the same SaaS templates. Skip the guidance and you get the same handful of tells on every project: Inter for everything, purple-to-blue gradients, cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, the rounded-square icon tile above every heading.

Impeccable adds:
- **One setup flow.** `/impeccable init` records durable product truth in `PRODUCT.md`, so later commands know the audience, purpose, operating context, constraints, voice, and evidence without confusing those facts with surface-level visual direction.
- **24 commands.** A shared design vocabulary with your AI: `polish`, `audit`, `critique`, `distill`, `animate`, `bolder`, `quieter`, and more.
- **62 deterministic detector rules** plus LLM-only critique checks. The CLI and browser extension run the deterministic rules with no LLM and no API key.

## What's Included

### The Skill: impeccable

The skill installs as one command:

```bash
/impeccable <command> <target>
```

Start every new project with:

```bash
/impeccable init
```

`init` inspects the project, asks only for material gaps in durable product truth, and writes `PRODUCT.md`. Visitor mode and visual direction are chosen later for each surface; incumbent or newly built visual systems are recorded separately in `DESIGN.md`.

### 24 Commands

All commands are accessed through `/impeccable`:

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `/impeccable craft` | F

Microduck

A tiny biped robot that moves using reinforcement learning policies.

Get yours here · Cheat sheet · Training the policies · How it works · Contributing

--- **This repo is the duck's brain.** About 25 cm and 800 g of robot, run by a handful of daemons on a Rockchip RK3566: a 50 Hz control loop driving fifteen servos from neural policies, the radios and the camera, and the update machinery that gets new software onto a robot without bricking it. Everything you need to run a Microduck is here. **If you want one, [get yours here](https://pollen-robotics.com/microduck).** The policies it runs are trained next door, in **[microduck_rl](https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck_rl)** — MuJoCo and PPO, the sim2real recipe, and the export to ONNX that this repo loads. ## It does things
It walks. Pick up a gamepad and drive. It rolls. Put wheels on, ask for roller mode, and it loads the other brain.

items.title: cloudflare/security-audit-skill
items.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings
items.readme:
# security-audit

A coding-agent skill that turns your agent into a security auditor. It orchestrates isolated agents through reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting.

This is the skill that seeded Cloudflare's vulnerability discovery harness, described in [Build your own vulnerability harness](https://blog.cloudflare.com/build-your-own-vulnerability-harness). The harness grew into a multi-stage, fleet-wide system; this skill is the single-repo starting point it evolved from.

## What it does

The skill runs a structured audit in six phases:

1. **Reconnaissance** -- map architecture, trust boundaries, input surfaces, prior evidence, and deterministic coverage in `architecture.md` and `coverage-ledger.json`.
2. **Coverage-led hunting** -- assign isolated hunters from ledger units, record their checks, and use coverage critics to find gaps.
3. **Candidate validation** -- give every unique candidate to a fresh verifier that tries to disprove it.
4. **Structured output** -- write `confirmed`, `needs_validation`, and `rejected` records to `findings.json` and validate them against `report-schema.json`.
5. **Independent record verification** -- fresh agents verify final source claims. Material replacements receive another independent verifier.
6. **Target-neutral reporting** -- derive `REPORT.md`, `FINDINGS-DETAIL.md`, and `NEEDS-VALIDATION.md` from the verified records and coverage ledger.

The parent runs `validate-coverage-ledger.cjs` after creating the ledger and after each later ledger update. It runs `validate-findings.cjs` in Phase 4 and again after every Phase 5 replacement.

The verdicts are distinct: `confirmed` has a complete source trace and bounded observed result, `needs_validation` has an exact unresolved fact and no severity, and `rejected` records a disproved candidate.

items.readme: # Ghidra Software Reverse Engineering Framework Ghidra is a software reverse engineering (SRE) framework created and maintained by the [National Security Agency][nsa] Research Directorate. This framework includes a suite of full-featured, high-end software analysis tools that enable users to analyze compiled code on a variety of platforms including Windows, macOS, and Linux. Capabilities include disassembly, assembly, decompilation, graphing, and scripting, along with hundreds of other features. Ghidra supports a wide variety of processor instruction sets and executable formats and can be run in both user-interactive and automated modes. Users may also develop their own Ghidra extension components and/or scripts using Java or Python. In support of NSA's Cybersecurity mission, Ghidra was built to solve scaling and teaming problems on complex SRE efforts, and to provide a customizable and extensible SRE research platform. NSA has applied Ghidra SRE capabilities to a variety of problems that involve analyzing malicious code and generating deep insights for SRE analysts who seek a better understanding of potential vulnerabilities in networks and systems. # Claude Code Plugins Directory

A curated directory of high-quality plugins for Claude Code.

> **⚠️ Important:** Make sure you trust a plugin before installing, updating, or using it. Anthropic does not control what MCP servers, files, or other software are included in plugins and cannot verify that they will work as intended or that they won't change. See each plugin's homepage for more information.

## Structure

- **`/plugins`** - Internal plugins developed and maintained by Anthropic
- **`/external_plugins`** - Third-party plugins from partners and the community

## Installation

Plugins can be installed directly from this marketplace via Claude Code's plugin system.

To install, run `/plugin install {plugin-name}@claude-plugins-official`

or browse for the plugin in `/plugin > Discover`

## Contributing

### Internal Plugins

Internal plugins are developed by Anthropic team members. See `/plugins/example-plugin` for a reference implementation.

### External Plugins

Third-party partners can submit plugins for inclusion in the marketplace. External plugins must meet quality and security standards for approval. To submit a new plugin, use the [plugin directory submission form](https://clau.de/plugin-directory-submission).

## Plugin Structure

Each plugin follows a standard structure:

```
plugin-name/
├── .claude-plugin/
│   └── plugin.json      # Plugin metadata (required)
├── .mcp.json            # MCP server configuration (optional)
├── commands/            # Slash commands (optional)
├── agents/              # Agent definitions (optional)
├── skills/              # Skill definitions (optional)
└── README.md            # Documentation
```

## Plugin names are immutable

The `name` field in a marketplace entry is an **immutable slug**. Once a plugin has been published, its `name` must not change — users have it installed under that slug, and renaming it breaks their install with a `plugin-not-found` error.

# Impeccable

Design guidance for AI coding agents. 1 skill, 24 commands, live browser iteration, and 62 deterministic detector rules for AI-generated frontend design.

> **Quick start:** From your project root, run `npx impeccable install`, then run `/impeccable init` inside your AI coding tool. Full docs: [impeccable.style](https://impeccable.style).

## Why Impeccable?

Anthropic's [frontend-design](https://github.com/anthropics/skills/tree/main/skills/frontend-design) was the first widely-used design skill for Claude. Impeccable started from there.

Every model trained on the same SaaS templates. Skip the guidance and you get the same handful of tells on every project: Inter for everything, purple-to-blue gradients, cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, the rounded-square icon tile above every heading.

Impeccable adds:
- **One setup flow.** `/impeccable init` records durable product truth in `PRODUCT.md`, so later commands know the audience, purpose, operating context, constraints, voice, and evidence without confusing those facts with surface-level visual direction.
- **24 commands.** A shared design vocabulary with your AI: `polish`, `audit`, `critique`, `distill`, `animate`, `bolder`, `quieter`, and more.
- **62 deterministic detector rules** plus LLM-only critique checks. The CLI and browser extension run the deterministic rules with no LLM and no API key.

# T3 Code

T3 Code is an "agent harness control surface". It enables control of the agents on your machine with a best-in-class mobile app ([iOS](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/t3-code-remote-claude-more/id6787819824), [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.t3tools.t3code)), [web app](https://app.t3.codes) and [Electron-based desktop app](https://t3.codes).

Works with your subscriptions on Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, and Google Antigravity. If they're set up on your computer, T3 Code can control them.

## "Wait, what are you selling me?"

Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar.

We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork and build the editor that you want.

## Installation

> [!WARNING]
> T3 Code currently supports Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, and Antigravity. Install and authenticate at least one provider before use:
>
> - Codex: install [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli) and run `codex login`
> - Claude: install [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code) and run `claude auth login`
> - Cursor: install [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/cli) and run `agent login`
> - Grok Build: install [Grok Build CLI](https://x.ai/cli) and run `grok login`
> - OpenCode: install [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) and run `opencode auth login`
> - Antigravity: enable it in Settings, then use **Install Antigravity** and **Sign in with Google**. No CLI is required.

items.readme:
# PageIndex: Vectorless, Reasoning-based RAG

Reasoning-based RAG  ◦  No Vector DB, No Chunking  ◦  Context-Aware Retrieval  ◦  Reads Like a Human

🌐 Website  •   ☁️ Cloud  •   📖 Docs  •   📝 Blog  •   ✉️ Contact 

Updates

 - [Aug '26] 🔥 [**PageIndex SDK**](#quickstart): **local** and **cloud** modes — one client to index, retrieve, and chat on your machine (with your own LLM API key) or on [PageIndex Cloud](https://developer.pageindex.ai/). - [Aug '26] ⚡ [**PageIndex Flash**](https://pageindex.ai/blog/pageindex-flash): fast tree index generation for text-based PDFs, now the default indexing method in PageIndex SDK local mode. - [Scale PageIndex to Millions of Documents](https://pageindex.ai/blog/pageindex-filesystem): *PageIndex File System* is a file-level tree indexing layer that lets PageIndex reason over an entire corpus, not just a single document. - [PageIndex App](https://app.pageindex.ai): a human-like document analysis agent for long professional documents.

items.title: Cursor 转 Codex 大半个月，聊聊我的真实感受
items.description: Cursor 让我第一次强烈感受到 AI 编程的震撼，Codex 则让我第一次真正感觉到，AI 不只是编程助手，而是一个真正的超级Agent，Codex 明显更接近下一阶段的形态。
items.summary_zh: 一位开发者记录了自己从 Cursor 转向 Codex、用了大半个月之后的体验：Cursor 让他第一次强烈感受到 AI 编程的冲击，而 Codex 更像一个能自己往下做事的超级 Agent，而非单纯的编程助手。这是主观使用感受而非基准测试，适合正在 Cursor 和 Codex 之间做选择、或关心 AI 编程工具形态往哪走的人参考。
items.summary_en: A developer who spent the better part of a month on Codex after switching from Cursor says the newer tool feels less like a coding assistant and more like a general-purpose agent that keeps working on its own, while Cursor was his first real taste of AI-assisted coding. It is a personal, hands-on account rather than a benchmark, useful for anyone choosing between the two or tracking how these tools are changing shape.

The article walks through what the project is and how to get started with it. Useful for anyone doing reverse engineering, security analysis, or binary inspection who wants a quick orientation before trying it out.

items.description: 35岁的程序员，是不是已经落幕了？ 最近一直在逛掘金的文章，有技术文章，有人生感悟，还有各种沸点。 看得越多，越觉得现在大家都不容易。 大环境的影响，加上 AI 的冲击，感觉整个行业正在进入一个落幕阶
items.summary_zh: 掘金上的一篇个人随笔，作者所在公司从 400 多人缩减到 100 多人，他借此重新思考程序员的未来，文中还提到 35 岁程序员的处境以及大环境和 AI 冲击带来的失落感。它不是技术教程，而是从业者对行业收缩期的观察，适合正在考虑职业规划的人读。
items.summary_en: A personal essay on Juejin whose author watched their company shrink from over 400 people to just over 100, and uses that to rethink the future of programmers, touching on the situation of 35-year-old developers and the combined pressure of a weak market and AI. It is not a technical tutorial but one developer's read on an industry in retreat, useful for anyone weighing career plans.

He frames it as a personal usage log rather than an ad or a hit piece, which makes it worth reading for developers comparing coding agents or thinking about leaving Codex.

items.summary_zh: 一位用 GPT 两年多、平时写方案改文案整理资料的重度用户，因为网络原因长期依赖第三方中转 API，这次记录了自己使用 WorkBuddy 一个月的真实体验。对同样靠中转站调用模型的开发者来说，这类长期使用反馈比发布会参数更有参考价值。

Devs who also reach models through relay endpoints will find this kind of long-term, hands-on account more useful than launch-day benchmarks.

items.title: 面试官问你：“AI 能写 80% 的代码了，公司为什么还需要你？”
items.description: 先说一个事实：2026 年的技术面试，已经和两年前完全不一样了。两年前面试问的是："手写一个 Promise"、"说说 React Fiber 原理"...现在面试官默认你会用 AI。他们真正想知道的
items.summary_zh: 这篇掘金文章讨论 2026 年技术面试的变化：两年前还在考手写 Promise、React Fiber 原理，如今面试官默认候选人会用 AI，转而追问「AI 能写 80% 的代码，公司为什么还需要你」。文章要回答的正是开发者该展示哪些 AI 替代不了的判断力和工程能力，适合正在准备面试的工程师。
items.summary_en: A Juejin post on how 2026 technical interviews differ from two years ago: instead of hand-writing a Promise or explaining React Fiber, interviewers now assume candidates already use AI and ask why a company should still hire them when AI writes 80% of the code. It's aimed at engineers preparing for interviews who need to articulate what AI can't replace.

items.title: 基于 Pi，我居然自己搞了一个好用的 AI Agent 桌面工作台
items.description: 先说结论：别重复造轮子 很多人一听"自己开发 Agent"，第一反应是"那不得从模型调用、消息循环、工具协议、权限系统一路手写？"。 其实不用。Ag
items.summary_zh: 这篇掘金文章的作者基于 Pi 搭了一个自用的 AI Agent 桌面工作台，核心主张是不要重复造轮子：模型调用、消息循环、工具协议、权限系统这些环节不必从零手写。它适合想自己动手做 Agent 桌面工具的开发者，重点在于如何复用已有能力，把精力放在工作台本身。
items.summary_en: A Juejin post describes how the author built an AI Agent desktop workbench on top of Pi. Its main argument is not to reinvent the wheel: the model calls, message loop, tool protocol and permission system do not need to be written from scratch. It is aimed at developers who want their own agent desktop tool without rebuilding the plumbing first.

items.title: 《别再“喂prompt赌运气”了：我的AI开发工程化管理实践》
items.description: 用AI写代码最怕什么？不是它写得慢，而是三个月后没人看得懂它写了什么。这篇文章不聊Prompt技巧，只讲一套被商业项目验证过的工程化管理方法：上下文冻结、阶段拆解、验收记录。

items.title: AI 都会写代码了，还要不要学传统编程了? （强烈建议阅读）
items.description: AI时代是否还需学编程？狂师指出：非技术人重在“会用”——懂基础概念、能说清需求、会简单验收；技术人则必须“会判”——语法基础不能丢，但重心转向读懂AI代码、判断质量与风险。写交给AI，责任留给人。
items.summary_zh: 掘金作者狂师把 AI 时代的编程能力拆成两类要求：非技术人重在“会用”，理解基础概念、把需求讲清楚、能做简单验收；技术人则要“会判”，语法基础不能丢，但重心转向读懂 AI 生成的代码并判断其质量与风险。核心主张是写代码可以交给 AI，责任仍由人承担。
items.summary_en: Writing on 掘金, author 狂师 splits programming skill in the AI era into two tracks: non-technical people need to "use" — grasp basic concepts, state requirements clearly and do light acceptance checks — while engineers need to "judge", keeping syntax fundamentals but shifting focus to reading AI-generated code and assessing its quality and risk. His claim is simple: let AI write, keep the responsibility human.

items.title: 我让 AI 独立开发了一款游戏：零依赖、188 个测试全绿、工期压到四分之一
items.description: 我用 AI 代码智能体独立开发了一款零运行时依赖的 Canvas 塔防游戏「熵减特勤局」，188 个测试全绿、一整局就是一个回归测试用例。本文讲清它解决的真实需求、开源与在线运营现状，以及开源加公众号

items.title: 老干妈靠AI闷赚54亿，你的AI还在写文案？
items.description: --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 每站填报表+会计录入 | 站长每天1小时填Excel，会计再1小时录财务软件，5个会计专职干这个 | 5个会计的工资，一年几十万 | 表格现
items.summary_zh: 文章借老干妈靠 AI 赚到 54 亿的说法切入，列举企业里填报表、财务录入这类重复劳动的代价：站长每天一小时填 Excel，会计再花一小时录入系统，5 个会计专职做这件事，一年工资几十万。作者想说的是，AI 该用在被流程吃掉的岗位上，而不只是写文案。
items.summary_en: Starting from the claim that Lao Gan Ma quietly earned 5.4 billion through AI, the piece tallies the cost of repetitive back-office work: site managers spend an hour a day filling Excel sheets, accountants spend another hour keying the data into finance software, and five full-time accountants exist just for that, costing hundreds of thousands a year in salaries. The argument is that AI belongs in these process-heavy roles, not just in copywriting.

items.summary_zh: 有开发者翻 GitHub Releases 页面发现 Spring AI Alibaba 的正式版停在 v1.1.2.2，于是技术群里就“项目是否已停更”吵了起来，文章由此讨论 Java 在 AI 应用方向还有没有机会。内容适合正在做 Java AI 技术栈选型、关心该项目维护状态的人。
items.summary_en: Developers noticed that Spring AI Alibaba's GitHub Releases page stops at v1.1.2.2, which set off a heated debate in tech groups over whether the project has halted updates and whether Java still has a future in AI applications. The article starts from that observation and digs into the project's release cadence and Java's AI options, for teams weighing a Java-based AI stack.

items.title: 我用 REA 逆向了付费颜色 APP，结果很意外！
items.description: GitHub 爆火的开源项目 REA 真的能逆向一切？软件已死？ 本期先科普什么是逆向工程、什么是 REA，然后实测用 AI 逆向单机安卓游戏和学习 App，看看它到底有没有那么神！
items.summary_zh: 这篇文章先解释逆向工程的基本概念和 GitHub 上走红的开源项目 REA，再动手用 AI 去逆一个单机 Android 游戏和一款学习类 App，看它在真实场景里能做到哪一步。适合想了解 AI 辅助逆向的实际边界、不满足于概念介绍的人。
items.summary_en: The post first explains what reverse engineering is and introduces REA, an open-source project that has drawn attention on GitHub, then uses it with AI against a single-player Android game and a learning app. It suits readers who want a hands-on look at where AI-assisted reverse engineering actually lands, rather than a purely conceptual overview.

items.title: 手机到底有没有偷听我们？我抓包了 72 小时，抓到了真凶
items.description: 麦克风硬件音频采集唤醒为 0 次；真正实现未卜先知的，是 公网 NAT 时空超图（ST-GNN）、现代隐私集合求交（PSI） 与 端侧微模型特征向量化（On-Device Em
items.summary_zh: 作者连续抓包 72 小时，发现麦克风硬件采集唤醒次数为 0，没有拿到手机偷听的证据；真正造成“未卜先知”的，是公网 NAT 时空超图（ST-GNN）、现代隐私集合求交（PSI）和端侧微模型特征向量化。适合关心隐私边界和推荐系统原理的开发者阅读。
items.summary_en: A developer captured 72 hours of phone traffic and found zero microphone wake-ups at the hardware level, which weakens the "my phone is listening" theory. The uncanny precognition instead traces to public NAT spatio-temporal hypergraphs (ST-GNN), modern private set intersection (PSI), and on-device micro-model feature vectorization. Useful for engineers who want to understand how targeting actually works and where the privacy line sits.

items.title: 2026，程序员的时代拐点到了
items.description: 未来的程序员，大概率不再是单纯坐在屏幕前敲代码的人，而是能调度AI、定义业务、兜底风险的人。AI不会精准淘汰某一个人，它只会把差距拉得更大。时代对愿意调整、持续精进的人，通常不吝啬。

items.title: 副业搞起来，小说，漫画，漫剧的成本优化思路

items.summary_en: A Juejin post laying out cost-optimization ideas for a side business built on novels, comics and comic-style shorts, linking the GitHub project aiskyhub/novel_to_comic for turning novels into comics. React 19.3 新增 browser() API，使“仅客户端渲染”成为一等公民
items.content: React 19.3 于 9 月 9 日在 npm 上发布 ，除了稳定的 View Transitions 和 Fragment Refs 外，还悄悄加入了一个规模较小但广受好评的新功能 react-dom browser() API ，允许组件正式选择不进行服务器端渲染。Aurora Scharff 分享了相关文档，并 宣布 该 API 已经上线，用户可以在 Canary 通道中使用：该通道将值传递给 use() 方法后，组件便会在服务器端暂停执行。 该功能针对的问题对任何从事服务器端渲染（SSR）的人来说都很熟悉。读取 localStorage、window 或设备时区的组件无法在服务器端生成有意义的 HTML，而现有的解决方法都比较笨拙。开发者要么在 effect 内部切换一个已挂载（mounted）标志，要么通过 typeof window !== ‘undefined’ 来控制渲染——当服务器端渲染与客户端首次渲染不一致时，这种模式会导致水合不匹配的问题。 新 API 取代了这两种方法： import { use } from 'react' ; import { browser } from 'react-dom' ; function LocalTime ( ) { use ( browser ()); return < p > {new Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone} </ p > ; } 复制代码 在服务器端渲染期间，use(browser()) 会暂停组件的渲染，并将最近的 Suspense 边界中的备用内容保留在 HTML 中。在浏览器中，它会返回 undefined，这样组件会在水合后正常渲染。该方法必须由客户端组件调用，并位于 Suspense 边界内，否则服务器端渲染会失败。由于 use() 可以位于条件表达式之后，所以组件仅在必要时才进行延迟渲染，例如，当加载器（loader）提供了 initialData 时，数据钩子会在服务器端进行渲染；否则，则选择跳过该渲染路径。React 还添加了 onBrowserBailout 回调函数和可选的 reason 参数，以便开发团队能够准确报告服务器端渲染被跳过的位置。 该变更最初以 React 核心 PR 的形式推出，This Week in React 将其 描述 为“消除了那些在服务器抑制错误的蹩脚的变通方案”。在跟踪该功能的 问题记录 中，一位贡献者写道，他们“对 browser() API 感到非常兴奋，因为它用比以往更简洁的方法解决了仅限客户端组件的问题”。在谈及此次发布时，一位开发者 称 ，对于“是否应在服务器端获取数据”这一难题，这种条件性数据获取是“我所见过的、最优雅的解决方案”。 该方案也缩小了与框架专属“逃生舱”机制之间的体验差距。长期以来，Next.js 用户一直通过 next/dynamic 使用 dynamic(() => import(‘./C’), { ssr: false })，而 Astro 则提供了 client:only 指令，但这两者都与各自的打包工具做了绑定。browser() 将这一功能整合到了 React 中，因此它适用于任何 SSR 配置，而不仅仅局限于单一框架。 升级只需要按照 React 19 升级指南 ，将版本号相应地调整为 react@19.3 和 react-dom@19.3 即可。不过， 用户指南 仍然将 browser() 标记为仅限 Canary 通道。因此，在生产环境中使用前，请先确认你的发布通道。 React 是一个用于构建用户界面的开源 JavaScript 库，最初由 Facebook 创建，目前由 Meta 联合庞大的贡献者社区共同维护。它推广了基于组件的模型，将用户界面描述为有状态的函数，并为 Next.js 和 Remix 等服务器端及全栈框架以及通过 React Native 构建的原生应用提供了技术支撑。自 2013 年首次发布以来，它已经成为使用最广泛的前端工具之一。最新版本进一步加强了服务器端渲染、Suspense 以及基于 browser() API 的并发功能。 声明：本文为 InfoQ 翻译，未经许可禁止转载。 原文链接： https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/10/react-19-3-browser-api/

items.title: 何时应使用 Liquid Clustering？湖仓布局策略基准测试
items.content: 简介 对于湖仓分析系统而言，并不存在一种放之四海皆准的最佳存储布局。在 Delta Lake 上针对四种工作负载类型进行的基准测试中，Liquid Clustering 在点查询、时间范围聚合和大型聚合方面均实现了最低延迟。对于查询模式多样或不断演变的团队而言，Liquid Clustering 应作为默认选择。ZOrdering 仅在稳定、高选择性的多谓词工作负载中表现更好，而且前提是过滤列与聚类键完全匹配。 在磁盘数据组织方面， 分区 、 ZOrdering 和 Liquid Clustering 各自采用了截然不同的方法；了解它们之间的权衡取舍，是你根据工作负载选择合适方案的关键。我有两项引人注目的发现，因为它们与通常对这些布局的描述相悖，而且可能正是这类问题在悄无声息地拖累生产系统的性能。 ZOrder 在日期范围处理上的隐性故障模式 当日期列在 ZOrder 聚簇表达式中作为二级或三级键时，与简单的按日期分区的表相比，时间范围查询的性能会差许多——在本基准测试中，其速度慢了 78%。连续的日期值分散在多个文件中，破坏了分区天然提供的范围扫描效率。如果你的团队对多个列做了 ZOrder 排序，而且日期并非第一个键，那么这几乎肯定会影响你的时间范围查询性能。 多列过滤器中 Liquid Clustering 的精度差距 当查询谓词能与一组稳定的过滤列精确匹配时，ZOrder 的文件剪枝效果接近最优，而 Liquid Clustering 在扫描多出十倍的数据时，运行速度可能变成五分之一。Liquid Clustering 采用更广泛的局部优化策略，以牺牲确定性剪枝为代价换取工作负载的灵活性。当查询范围狭窄而且可预测时，这种权衡恰恰会成为一种负担。 这些测试结果之所以重要，是因为物理数据布局是湖仓工程中影响最为深远却鲜少被讨论的决策之一，而分区、ZOrdering 和 Liquid Clustering 之间的权衡通常仅从概念上进行了描述，并没有通过实际测量来验证。 大多数已经发表的对比研究要么来自 Databricks 自己，要么是基于第一性原理推导出的权衡分析，并未针对实际的查询行为进行度量。本次基准测试所探讨的问题，直接源于我在 TCS 英国分公司（民用航空航天领域）和 IBM（壳牌海事）设计 Delta Lake 平台时实际遇到的生产挑战。在这些场景中，数据布局决策会直接影响管道服务水平协议（SLA）的合规性以及云计算的成本。 我的实际建议是：在确定布局策略之前，请针对你自身数据的一个具有代表性的样本，将最常用的三种查询模式分别应用于分区、ZOrdered 和 Liquid Clustered 这三种配置。下面的结果来自一项受控基准测试。该测试使用真实的 Databricks 查询配置文件，在包含 5000 万条记录的数据集上，针对四种分析型工作负载类型对这三种布局策略进行了比较。这些结果可能会让你感到惊讶，就像当初让我感到惊讶一样。 这在实践中意味着什么 综合来看，这些测试结果基于工作负载类型勾勒出了一个清晰的决策框架： 本文中最具实践价值的见解，或许是一个看似简单却极具洞察力的诊断性问题——在确定任何布局策略之前，实践者都应该自问：我的热门查询是否总是根据相同的两到三个列进行筛选？仅凭对这一问题的回答，就能判断复合分区究竟能带来实质性的收益，还是会引入不必要的复杂性。 如果答案是“是”，即这些列是已知的而且很稳定，那么就应该仅对这些列使用 ZOrder，从而确保选择性最高的列排在首位。如果答案是否定的，或者查询模式可能发生变化，那么就应该将 Liquid Clustering 设为默认选项。在四种工作负载类型中，Liquid Clustering 在其中三种中表现更优，并且消除了手动调度 OPTIMIZE 带来的运维开销。 GitHub 上提供了一个用 Python 编写的决策辅助工具。 下文将详细阐述这些建议背后的方法论、结果和分析，即如何和为何，供希望在应用这些发现之前进行验证的读者参考。 实验设置 以下是数据集、布局配置、工作负载以及分析结果。 数据集 我们生成了一组包含五千万条记录的合成事务数据集，用于模拟零售购买环境，其数据模式如下： customer_id INT uniform distribution, range 12 , 000 , 000 txn_date
